lines.text: A gold coin you cannot lift.
The Perth Mint made a gold coin that weighs 1,012 kilograms.
lines.say: The Perth Mint made a gold coin that weighs one thousand twelve kilograms.

lines.text: It is 80 centimeters wide and 99.99 percent pure gold.
lines.say: It is eighty centimeters wide and ninety nine point nine nine percent pure gold.

lines.text: As legal tender, its face value is one million Australian dollars.
The design is a leaping kangaroo by goldsmith Stuart Devlin.
The same design is on the mint's smaller one kilogram coins.
It was made to promote the mint's Kangaroo gold coin series.
In 2012, Guinness named it the largest coin in the world.
lines.say: In twenty twelve, Guinness named it the largest coin in the world.

lines.text: It once stood outside the New York Stock Exchange.
It is kept in the Gold Exhibition at the Perth Mint.
